entry.title: Play with the things already here
entry.summary: Davies makes room at home for open-ended play as well as practical activities. Familiar favorites can be a good place to begin.
entry.cue: Your child may be exploring a familiar toy in a new way.
detail: At home, Davies makes room for imaginative scenes from daily life. In her separate creativity discussion, she describes pretend play as processing experience and places its beginning around 2½ years and later.

Her home examples include blocks, farm animals, trains, and vehicles. These are possibilities within a varied collection, not a shopping list. Materials still need to fit the child using them, with supervision for small parts.
If a child attends a Montessori classroom, she makes room at home for daily life, outdoors, creativity, and rest without duplicating all the school materials.

references.locator: Open-ended toys, everyday imaginative play, existing favorites, storage/rotation and home/school distinction
Imagination, pretend play around 2½ years and later, and artistic creativity

ageContext.bookAge: Home play is unaged within the toddler chapter; the separate creativity discussion places pretend play around 2.5+ years.
ageContext.readiness: Interest in open-ended familiar toys; later pretend play can draw on real daily experience.
ageContext.note: The start of this band does not imply pretend play should have begun; Davies’s later description remains around 2½ and older.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
